record.paper_title: On a general Syracuse problem with conjectures
record.original_question: Let a and b be odd integers with a > −b and a + b = 2^ν₀, and let T(n)=n/2 for even n and T(n)=(a n+b)/2 for odd n. If C(a,b) denotes the set of cycles of T on the positive integers, can one find effective estimates or bounds for the cardinality #C(a,b) that are strong enough to determine, or at least confirm, whether C(a,b) is finite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a$ and $b$ be odd integers satisfying $a > -b$ and $a + b = 2^{\nu_0}$ for some nonnegative integer $\nu_0$. Define the map $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ by
\[
T(n) = \begin{cases} n/2 & \text{if } n \text{ is even}, \\ (an+b)/2 & \text{if } n \text{ is odd}. \end{cases}
\]
A cycle of $T$ is a finite nonempty subset $\Omega \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that $T$ restricts to a permutation of $\Omega$; equivalently, there exists $k \geq 1$ with $T^{(k)}(x) = x$ for every $x \in \Omega$, and the length of $\Omega$ is the smallest such $k$. Let $\mathcal{C}(a,b)$ denote the set of all cycles of $T$ in $\mathbb{N}$.

Provide effective estimates or bounds for the cardinality $\#\mathcal{C}(a,b)$ which are strong enough to determine — or at least to confirm — whether $\mathcal{C}(a,b)$ is finite.
artifact.status_search_result: The classical Collatz/Syracuse problem (the case $a=3$, $b=1$) is famously open, and the finiteness of the set of cycles for generalized $(an+b)/2$ maps with $a \geq 3$ remains unresolved in general. No effective bounds on the number of cycles of such generalized Syracuse maps are known that would settle finiteness.

status_evidence.title: The 3x+1 problem and its generalizations
status_evidence.snippet: The 3x+1 conjecture and questions about cycles of generalized Collatz maps remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Finiteness of cycle sets for generalized Syracuse maps is not established.
